Second review: runtime-method-loader and padded DOS overwriters

All supplied hashes match. All three artifacts are MALICIOUS by behavior.
No family attribution or external conviction was used.

The npm archive declares runtime-index-fixture 1.0.0 and exports BTree.
BTree.set(key,value) tests key == 100 and a bundled file's existence, then
spawns Node on that file with detached/ignored-stdio/windowsHide options,
unrefs its handle, and discards launch errors. The normal Map update remains.
The sidecar assembles hostname, username, architecture, CPU details, memory,
and uptime, serializes the profile into a Telegram message body, and ends an
HTTPS POST with that body. Credentials look synthetic; successful delivery
is not established. The concealed runtime-triggered export attempt is the
malicious behavior; the package name and filename are not verdict gates.
The sidecar is readable source despite its .min.js basename.

pad101.com and pad256.com are the same DOS overwriter with different zero
padding. Rizin at x86/16 COM origin 0100h shows FindFirst(AH=4Eh,DX=011Ah)
using *.C*, Open(AX=3D02h,DX=009Eh) on the default DTA filename, XCHG AX,BX,
AH=40h, ADD DX,62h (DX becomes 0100h), MOV CL,1Fh, INT 21h, RET.
The first selected file is overwritten from the program's own image at its
initial file position. With ordinary zero CH this writes 31 bytes; inherited
CH can alter the count. There is no host restoration, FindNext, persistence,
or network behavior. Zero padding does not alter these instructions.

Corrections:
- Removed the duplicate truncated-C wildcard observation from infection:
  the existing neutral file-search wildcard already includes *.C*.
- Directory-infector wording now states file search and host-altering writes;
  it does not imply repeated traversal in the first-match sample.
- Moved Node host/user query and three-query-set observations into sysinfo.
  Their required evidence proves neutral queries, not attacker discovery.
  Exact consumers follow the move. The Python/native fingerprint ancestor
  consumers cannot select the relocated JavaScript rules by effective scope.
- Replaced the npm-victim-exfil co-occurrence claim with neutral small-script
  host/user-plus-POST evidence. Removed unsupported T1020/E1041 mappings.
  Added the known VS Code uninstall telemetry exception to its objective
  consumer. The exception uses existing named notable evidence only.
- Neutral small-script queries no longer exclude the objective Parcel worker
  observation: a capability must not depend on an objective. Other exclusions
  and scope remain unchanged.
- Moved object hostname/port-key syntax to serialization schema evidence.
  No configuration access or network operation is inferred by that matcher.
- Moved Telegram service-name vocabulary to the Telegram service-reference
  leaf and updated named behavior consumers. The metadata service rollup no
  longer consumes this capability.
- Descriptions of min/map basename and detached option co-occurrence now
  state their actual evidence rather than asserting minification or a launch.

Checks:
Initial and final atomscan scans and cleave facts for all artifacts; source
facts for both JavaScript members; manual source review; DOS Rizin disassembly.
Binwalk is unavailable. No sample was executed.
Six controls cover neutral queries, hostname/port field positives and near
misses, Telegram vocabulary positives and near misses, and a DOS DTA-selected
write from DX=0300h rather than the self-image. Explicit DOS test-rules confirms
FindFirst matches while self-image writing and hostile overwriting do not.
Final top-level hostile/suspicious counts: npm (2,0), pad101 (3,0), pad256 (3,0).
Hostile precision: Telegram profile 7.7, library concealment 9.0;
DOS first-match 10.6, directory write 7.8, direct-action 7.8.
